title: Request-byte telemetry counts the pre-SDK dictionary instead of the transmitted JSON body
rationale: Every successful stage computes request_bytes from the Python keyword dictionary before AsyncOpenAI transforms it. The dictionary includes SDK-only extra_body nesting and default JSON spacing; the SDK merges extra_body into the body and HTTPX serializes compact JSON. A read-only reproduction using the installed real OpenAI 2.54.0 SDK, HTTPX MockTransport, stage=review, MatchingResult, synthetic instructions/text and no images reported 1013 bytes while the actual captured HTTP body was 912 bytes. Thus the newly added count does not satisfy AC-S05's actual-request-byte accounting and cannot be used as measured wire-body evidence. This is a telemetry-only defect: the counter does not enforce the 512 KiB payload limit, and no capacity bypass or model failure is claimed. The new test compares against the same pre-SDK request dictionary, so it passes despite this mismatch.
suggestion: Measure the serialized HTTP request body at the SDK/transport boundary without retaining or logging content. Keep payload/image counts separate. Add an exact equality assertion against a real SDK request captured by a local MockTransport, including extra_body, Unicode and images; do not equate a pre-SDK JSON estimate with actual transmitted bytes.
